en.title: Why Atlas Air broke three decades of Boeing loyalty for the Airbus A350F
en.summary: Atlas Air, the world's largest operator of Boeing 747 freighters, has ordered Airbus A350F freighters for the first time in its history, a shift driven by delays to Boeing's 777-8F and the need to replace its ageing 747 fleet between 2029 and 2034.
body: Atlas Air's fleet is built entirely around Boeing widebodies: as of 2026 it operates 113 aircraft, including 59 Boeing 747s, 23 767-300s and 11 777s, plus four specialised Dreamlifter transports and eight converted 737-800s flown for Amazon. That all-Boeing line-up, dating back to the early 1990s, gives Atlas about 13% of the global widebody freighter fleet and makes it the world's largest heavy air cargo operator. On March 16 Atlas ordered 20 Airbus A350F freighters, with options for 20 more, and added 20 further purchase rights in October, giving it a path to as many as 60 Airbus freighters.

The decisive factor was time. Boeing's 777-8F has not yet been certified by the US Federal Aviation Administration, so Atlas could not obtain firm delivery guarantees, and with the passenger 777-9's entry into service slipping to 2027, the freighter's debut is now estimated around 2029 or 2030. The A350Fs are scheduled to replace 747s between 2029 and 2034, while the 747-8F subfleet, whose final airframes were accepted in early 2023, would keep handling outsized cargo that cannot fit through side doors. Atlas has nevertheless left room for the 777-8F in later fleet renewal rounds, and the A350F's wider main-deck cargo door and the 777-8F's wider fuselage each solve a different part of the post-747 cargo problem.

facts.claim: Atlas Air ordered 20 Airbus A350F freighters on March 16, with options for 20 more, and added 20 further purchase rights in October.
As of 2026 Atlas operates 113 aircraft, all Boeing widebody freighters, including 59 Boeing 747s, and holds about 13% of the global widebody freighter fleet.
Atlas also flies four specialised Dreamlifter transports used to ferry large 787 components between Boeing manufacturing sites.
The A350Fs are scheduled to replace 747s between 2029 and 2034 as Atlas retires its ageing quadjets.
Boeing's 777-8F has not yet been fully certified by the Federal Aviation Administration, and its debut is currently estimated around 2029 or 2030.
Atlas accepted its final production Boeing 747-8Fs in early 2023.

zh.title: Atlas航空為何打破30年波音忠誠轉向空中巴士A350F
zh.summary: 全球最大波音747貨機營運商Atlas航空首度訂購空中巴士A350F貨機，主因是波音777-8F延宕且無法保證交機時程，而老舊747機隊須在2029年至2034年間汰換。
body: Atlas航空的機隊完全圍繞波音廣體機建立：截至2026年共營運113架飛機，包括59架波音747、23架767-300與11架777，另有4架專門運送波音787大型組件的Dreamlifter運輸機，以及8架為亞馬遜國內運輸改裝的737-800。這支自1990年代初期延續至今的全波音機隊，讓Atlas握有全球廣體貨機機隊約13%，成為全球最大的重型航空貨運營運商。Atlas於3月16日訂購20架空中巴士A350F貨機並取得20架選擇權，10月再增加20架購買權，未來最多可擁有60架空中巴士貨機。

關鍵因素是時間。波音777-8F尚未獲得美國聯邦航空總署完整認證，Atlas無法取得確切的交機保證，而客運版777-9投入服務已推遲至2027年，貨機版首飛目前預估落在2029年或2030年。A350F預定在2029年至2034年間汰換747，至於2023年初才接收最後一批生產機的747-8F機隊，則繼續承擔無法從側門裝載的超大貨物。儘管如此，Atlas仍為後續機隊更新保留777-8F的空間，而A350F更寬的主貨艙門與777-8F更寬的機身，正好各自解決747退役後不同的貨運難題。
